steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and spray a sheet pan with nonstick spray.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper and pour onto the pan.
Bake 10–12 minutes until starting to set, then pull out the rack and stir with a spatula.
Bake about 8–10 minutes more until set how you like, then stir, fluff and season.
Serve hot with toppings, or cool and store airtight up to 4 days.
recipes.title: Oven Baked Scrambled Eggs (Meal Prep)

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1 inch thick)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a rimmed sheet with parchment.
Mix the spices. Rub the chicken with the oil, then the spices.
Bake 20 minutes.
Brush both sides with half the BBQ sauce and bake 10 minutes.
Brush the tops with the rest and bake 10–15 minutes to 160°F. Rest 5–10 minutes.
recipes.title: Oven Roasted BBQ Chicken

ingredients.item: cumin, cinnamon, garam masala, ground coriander, turmeric, salt, smoked paprika

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Asian. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate (with bone).
steps: Mix the ginger, garlic, spices, salt, oil and yogurt.
Pat the chicken dry and coat it completely in the marinade. Marinate 10 minutes at room temperature or up to a day in the fridge.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and set wire racks over foil-lined sheets.
Shake off the excess marinade and bake 20–25 minutes until charred at the edges and 165°F inside.
Rest 5 minutes.
recipes.title: Oven-Baked Tandoori Chicken

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. This is Pioneer Woman's recipe as shared by Mormon Mavens. Use a dense bread; regular sandwich bread turns soggy. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Butter a 9x13 pan and tear the bread into bite-size chunks in it.
Mix the eggs, milk, cream, sugar and vanilla and pour evenly over the bread. Cover tightly and refrigerate several hours or overnight.
Mix the flour, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt, and cut in the butter until crumbly like small pebbles. Refrigerate in a zip bag.
To bake, uncover, sprinkle the crumbs evenly on top, and bake at 350°F for 1 hour (45 minutes for softer, more pudding-like).
Serve with syrup or a quick powdered sugar and milk glaze.
recipes.title: Overnight Baked French Toast with Crumb Topping

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Lunch. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Layer the rice, beans, vegetables, salsa and cheese in a microwave-safe container and cover tightly.
Keep chilled (don't leave out more than 6 hours). Microwave on full power 3–4 minutes to serve.
recipes.title: Packed Lunch Rice & Bean Bowl

ingredients.item: pine nuts or walnuts (coconut flakes or none for AIP)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. Makes 2 cups. Calories, protein and weight are estimates per 2 tbsp.
steps: Pulse the walnuts a few times (skip for pine nuts).
Add the basil and pulse, then the garlic and the nutritional yeast if using.
Stream in the oil with the processor running and salt to taste.
recipes.title: Paleo (and AIP) Pesto

ingredients.item: beef stew meat, 1-inch chunks, patted dry
dried shiitake mushrooms, ground to a powder

recipes.notes: From the 40 Aprons roundup Whole30 Slow Cooker Recipes. Freezes well. The site lists 203 kcal and 4 g protein, which looks wrong for 2 lb of beef, so calories, protein and weight here are my estimates.
steps: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Brown the beef in batches without crowding, salting each side, about 5 minutes per side. Set aside.
Add the carrots, celery, onion and garlic with 1/4 cup stock, 1 tsp salt and pepper, scraping up the browned bits. Cook until softened and browning, 5–10 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and mushroom powder.
Add the remaining stock, the potatoes, thyme and bay leaves, and the beef.
Move everything to the slow cooker and cook on HIGH at least 6 hours (or cover and bake in a 300°F oven 6 hours).
Turn off the heat 5 minutes before serving, remove the bay leaves and stir in the peas. Season and serve.
recipes.title: Paleo + Whole30 Beef Stew

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories and protein are the site's figures, including the potatoes; time and weight are estimates.
steps: Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, adding the sage and fennel as it cooks. Move it to a plate.
Make sure there's about 3 tbsp fat in the pan (add coconut oil, ghee or bacon grease if needed).
Stir the almond and tapioca flours into the fat over medium heat.
Stir in the milk and cook until thick, whisking if needed.
Return the sausage and serve right away over the potatoes.
recipes.title: Paleo / Whole30 Sausage Gravy over Potatoes

ingredients.item: macaroni (cassava pasta for AIP, or rice pasta)
fresh thyme, sage, rosemary or parsley, to garnish

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Cook the pasta per the package (about 11 minutes), save 1 cup cooking water, drain, and return the water and pasta to the pot off the heat.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil with 1/2 tsp salt over medium 5–8 minutes until wilted, then cover on low 10 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Brown the beef with the remaining salt about 6 minutes.
Lower the heat, add the garlic, fresh and dried ginger and herbs for 1 minute, and return the mushrooms.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer 2–3 minutes.
Gently toss the sauce with the pasta and garnish with fresh herbs.
recipes.title: Paleo AIP Hamburger Macaroni

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories and protein are the site's figures per muffin; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Purée the bananas in a food processor or blender as smooth as you like.
Add the almond butter, coconut oil, eggs, maple syrup and vanilla and pulse until smooth.
Add the almond flour, baking soda and salt and pulse just until combined.
Scoop into a greased or nonstick muffin tin.
Bake 20–22 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Repeat with the remaining batter.
recipes.title: Paleo Almond Butter Banana Muffins

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13.
Cook the onion and mushrooms with the salt in the coconut oil 5–10 minutes until soft.
Wring the squash dry in a clean towel, in batches.
Brown the meats in the pan, then stir in the sauce. Off the heat, add the tomatoes and basil.
In a large bowl, combine with the squash and the beaten eggs.
Spread in the pan, top with pepperoni, and bake 45 minutes.
recipes.title: Paleo Baked Spaghetti (Spaghetti Squash)

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken thighs, bite-size pieces

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. The site doesn't say how many it serves; the numbers here assume 2 1/2 lb chicken and 1 1/2 cans coconut milk over 6 servings. The recipe lists almonds and cilantro without saying where they go, so I put them on top. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Melt the ghee in a large pot over medium and cook the onions with the salt until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, paprika and cayenne and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, scraping up the spices.
Add the chicken and cook through.
Stir in the coconut milk and garam masala and heat through. Top with almonds and cilantro.
recipes.title: Paleo Butter Chicken

ingredients.item: cassava flour, whisked then spooned in
non-hydrogenated vegetable or palm shortening, room temp
milk (full-fat coconut milk for dairy-free), room temp

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. The live page didn't load the recipe, so this comes from a 2022 web archive copy. Calories, protein, weight and the number of biscuits are estimates.
steps: Preheat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet.
Put the lemon juice in a 1-cup measure and fill with milk; set aside.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then cut in the shortening to coarse crumbs.
Stir in the soured milk until a dough forms, pressing it together, then gather it into a ball (it stops being sticky).
Pat out between floured parchment to 3/4–1 inch thick. Cut straight down with a floured cutter (don't twist) and place close together. Re-roll the scraps.
Smooth each top with a fingertip of water and bake about 14–18 minutes for 2-inch biscuits, until golden.
recipes.title: Paleo Cassava Flour Biscuits

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. Calories are the site's figure; the site's protein figure is clearly wrong, so protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Whisk the almond milk and vinegar and let stand 10 minutes.
Mix the cassava flour and baking powder in a large bowl.
Whisk the almond butter and maple syrup into the milk, then mix into the dry ingredients until smooth.
Pour about 1/8 cup batter per pancake into a well-heated nonstick pan and cook over medium until bubbles appear and the bottom browns. Flip and cook 1–2 minutes.
Serve with berries or maple syrup.
recipes.title: Paleo Cassava Flour Pancakes (Vegan, Oil-Free)

ingredients.item: yellow or butternut squash, small cubes

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Sides. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Steam the cauliflower: Instant Pot on Steam 6 minutes with 1 cup water, or covered in a large pan with the ghee, salt and 1/2 cup water until tender.
Sauce: melt the ghee and sauté the squash, carrot, onion, garlic powder, mustard and salt 5 minutes until the onion is translucent.
Add the coconut milk and simmer about 10 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the milk has reduced by two-thirds.
Blend very smooth, then immediately blend in the egg yolk (the heat cooks and thickens it).
Season and toss with the hot cauliflower.
recipes.title: Paleo Cauliflower Mac and Cheese

ingredients.item: cauliflower florets (1/2 small head), or 2 medium carrots, chopped
herbs, e.g. fresh basil and thyme (optional)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. The recipe says 6 rounds but the steps say 4–5; nutrition here is per round, out of 6. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Pulse the cauliflower (or carrots) and coconut flour in a food processor 30–60 seconds into crumbs, then add everything else and blend until smooth, about a minute.
Form into rounds a little thicker than 1/4 inch (dampen your hands to flatten them).
Sprinkle with sesame seeds if you like.
Bake 15–17 minutes until lightly browned underneath and dry on top, flip, and bake 3 minutes more until firm. Cool a few minutes before lifting off. Best the day they're made.
recipes.title: Paleo Cauliflower Sandwich Rounds

ingredients.item: coconut milk (or other unsweetened nut milk)
berries, plus more to top (e.g. blueberries)
optional toppings: other fresh fruit, toasted coconut, grain-free granola

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories, protein and weight are estimates (protein assumes the collagen).
steps: Whisk the chia seeds, milk, salt, and collagen and vanilla if using, stirring until the seeds start to swell and it thickens. Set aside.
Cook the berries in a small pan over medium heat, stirring often, until they break down and get saucy.
Layer the berries and chia pudding in a small jar, add any toppings, cover and refrigerate. Eat cold, or warm 30 seconds.
recipes.title: Paleo Chia Seed Pudding with Warm Berries

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Smoothies. Calories and protein are the site's figures (the protein looks low with collagen added); weight is an estimate.
steps: Add everything to a high-power blender in the order listed and blend smooth.
recipes.title: Paleo Chocolate Coconut Smoothie

ingredients.item: coconut sugar or raw cane sugar

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 of 10).
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Line a 9” x 5” loaf pan with parchment paper.

Add the ingredients for the banana bread to a blender and blend until smooth (note: you can prepare the batter in a mixing bowl by mashing and stirring everything together if you don’t have a high-powered blender).
In a mixing bowl, stir together the ingredients for the cinnamon swirl mixture until well-combined and set aside until ready to use.
Pour half of the banana bread batter into the parchment lined loaf pan, and sprinkle with half of the cinnamon swirl mixture.
Pour the remaining banana bread batter on top and smooth into an even layer. Sprinkle the remaining streusel topping on top.

Bake on the center rack of the preheated oven for 45 minutes. Remove the bread from the oven and cover it in foil. Place it back in the oven and bake another 15 to 20 minutes, or until the bread is cooked through. Insert a digital thermometer into the center of the bread. If the internal temperature is 190 degrees F or higher, it is ready!
Allow the banana bread to cool to room temperature before slicing and serving.
recipes.title: Paleo Cinnamon Swirl Banana Bread

ingredients.item: ghee (coconut oil for AIP or vegan)
bone broth (or vegetable broth or water)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Grate the cauliflower into rice-size pieces.
Heat a 6-quart Instant Pot on Sauté 5 minutes, add the fat, and cook the shallot and garlic 4–5 minutes.
Add the squash, salt and pepper and sauté 8 minutes.
Turn off Sauté and stir in the cauliflower, nutritional yeast, coconut milk and broth.
Seal and cook on Manual 2 minutes, then quick release.
Sprinkle in the tapioca and stir until thick (drain extra liquid if needed). Season and stir in the sage.
recipes.title: Paleo Instant Pot Butternut Squash Risotto (Cauliflower Rice)

ingredients.item: ground Italian sausage or ground beef (meatballs)

recipes.notes: From the Beauty and the Foodie roundup Low Carb Slow Cooker Meals. Calories and protein are the site's figures; serving weight is an estimate.
steps: Knead all the meatball ingredients together by hand.
Roll into tablespoon-size meatballs and brown on all sides in a greased skillet over medium-high heat (they needn't cook through).
Set the slow cooker to HIGH and put the pancetta and garlic in the bottom.
Add the meatballs.
Add the broth, tomatoes, zucchini, squash, carrot, onion, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and salt.
Cook on HIGH 5 hours or LOW 8 (or HIGH 4 then LOW 2).
Serve garnished with Parmesan if you eat dairy.
recipes.title: Paleo Italian Meatball Soup

recipes.notes: DOUBLE SAUCE. From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Asian. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Salt the sliced chicken and toss it in the arrowroot.
Cook in the oil in a large pan over medium 4–6 minutes, stirring, to 165°F. Set aside.
Lower to medium-low and cook the ginger and garlic 2–3 minutes.
Whisk in the coconut aminos, broth, pepper and coconut sugar and cook 2–3 minutes until thick.
Return the chicken, stir to coat, and add the green onions 1–2 minutes. Serve with cauliflower rice.
recipes.title: Paleo Mongolian Chicken (Whole30, AIP)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Soup. The blog has moved to realfoodwithjessica.com (same author), and the old link redirects there. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Combine everything in a large saucepan.
Cook over medium 30 minutes until the onions and mushrooms are soft.
Season and serve. Great as leftovers.
recipes.title: Paleo Pizza Soup

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Preheat oven to 325° and line a 9x9 pan with parchment paper.
Make the crumb topping first: in a small bowl, combine coconut flour, almond flour, coconut sugar, cinnamon, maple syrup, and coconut oil. Mix well- it should resemble wet sand. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine coconut oil, maple syrup, coconut sugar, and pumpkin. Mix well.
Add in the eggs and mix until incorporated.
Add in the almond flour, coconut flour, baking soda, pumpkin spice, cinnamon, and salt. Mix until no dry pockets remain. Pour into prepared pan and top with crumb topping.
Bake for 45-50 minutes.
Store in fridge after the first day.
recipes.title: Paleo Pumpkin Coffee Cake

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Snacks. Calories and protein are the site's figures per mini muffin; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a 24-cup mini muffin pan well.
Blend everything in a food processor until completely smooth.
Fill the cups almost to the top with a small scoop and bake 20 minutes until golden.
recipes.title: Paleo Pumpkin Protein Mini Muffins

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a muffin pan.
Mix the coconut flour, almond flour, cinnamon, pumpkin spice, baking soda, baking powder and salt.
Blend the zucchini, pumpkin, coconut sugar and coconut oil in a blender or food processor until smooth.
Blend in the vanilla and vinegar, then the dry ingredients.
Add the eggs all at once and blend just until combined. Stir in the chips by hand.
Scoop 1/4 cup batter into each cup.
Bake 20–25 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean (or bake as a 9x5 loaf for 35–40 minutes).
recipes.title: Paleo Pumpkin Zucchini Muffins

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Sides. Makes 1 cup. Calories and weight are estimates per tablespoon.
steps: Whisk everything until the mayo and coconut milk are fully combined.
Keeps a week in the fridge in an airtight container.
recipes.title: Paleo Ranch Dressing (Whole30, Dairy-Free)

ingredients.item: diced tomatoes with basil and garlic

recipes.notes: From the Meal Prep on Fleek roundup 31 Slow Cooker Meal Prep Recipes. Calories and protein are the site's figures; serving weight is an estimate.
steps: Mix the almond flour, 1/2 tsp salt, onion and garlic powders, Italian seasoning and red pepper.
Sprinkle the beef with the remaining salt, add the egg, the almond flour mix and parsley, and mix gently by hand just until combined.
Line a baking sheet with parchment, preheat the broiler, and shape 20 meatballs.
Broil 2–4 minutes to lightly brown and release some fat.
Move the meatballs to the slow cooker, leaving the fat behind. Add all the sauce ingredients and stir gently.
Cover and cook on LOW 4 hours, until cooked through.
Serve over sweet potato or zucchini noodles, or with roasted vegetables. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge or a month frozen.
recipes.title: Paleo Slow Cooker Meatballs in Marinara

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Serves 6–12. Calories and protein are the site's figures for 6 servings; weight is an estimate.
steps: Sauce: steam the cauliflower 8 minutes until soft, then blend smooth with the ghee, broth, mustard and salt (thin with more broth if needed).
Meatballs: mix everything by hand and roll 1 1/2–2 inch balls.
Brown in the oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high in 2–3 batches, about 2 minutes per side.
Wipe out the pan, lower to medium-low, bring the sauce to a gentle boil, add the meatballs, cover and cook 5–8 minutes until cooked through (or simmer 30+ minutes for deeper flavor).
recipes.title: Paleo Swedish Meatballs (Creamy Cauliflower Sauce)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Calories and protein are the site's figures, including the potatoes; weight is an estimate.
steps: Mash: boil the potatoes in salted water until very soft, drain, and mash over low heat with the ghee and coconut milk. Season, adding nutritional yeast if you like.
Cook the onion in 1 tbsp ghee in a large nonstick skillet until soft; cool slightly.
Mix the onion with the rest of the meatball ingredients without overworking, and form 1 1/2-inch balls.
Brown the meatballs in the skillet, turning carefully, then set aside.
Gravy: melt 3 tbsp ghee, whisk in the arrowroot until bubbly, add the remaining gravy ingredients, and bring to a strong simmer.
Return the meatballs and simmer 3–5 minutes until cooked through and the gravy thickens. Serve over the mashed potatoes.
recipes.title: Paleo Swedish Meatballs with Mashed Potatoes (Whole30)

ingredients.item: grass-fed ground beef or ground turkey

recipes.notes: From Pinterest board Foods I do like. Kids especially like this one. Calories, protein and weight are estimates (1 whole sweet potato per serving, 85/15 beef).
steps: Sauté the onion, garlic and celery in a skillet until the onion is tender.
Add the ground beef and brown it.
Add the spices, coconut sugar (or honey) and bell peppers.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their liquid and the tomato paste.
Simmer on low about 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Halve the sweet potatoes and scoop out a little to make a bowl, then fill with the sloppy joe mix (or cut into wedges and spoon the mix over).
Serve hot.
recipes.title: Paleo Sweet Potato Sloppy Joes

ingredients.item: dry white wine (more for a saucier sauce)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Sauce: warm the oil over medium and cook the pepper flakes and garlic 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 8–12 minutes until soft and blistered but holding their shape.
Add the wine and bring to a gentle simmer, then stir in the basil, lemon juice and zest, salt, sugar and pepper and cook 2 minutes. Set aside.
Pat the cod dry, season, and cook in the oil in a nonstick pan over medium about 3 minutes until golden. Flip and cook 3–4 minutes more.
Pour the sauce over, warm a minute, and serve.
recipes.title: Pan-Seared Cod in White Wine Tomato Basil Sauce

ingredients.item: New York strip (or ribeye or top sirloin)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. A serving is half a steak. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Pat the steaks very dry and season with the salt and pepper just before cooking.
Heat a cast iron pan, add the oil over medium-high, and sear the steaks 4 minutes until crusted. Flip and cook 3–4 minutes more, searing the fat edge with tongs.
Lower to medium, add the butter, garlic and rosemary, and spoon the butter over the steaks about a minute, until 5–10°F under your target.
Rest 10 minutes loosely covered, slice 1/2 inch thick, and spoon the butter over.
recipes.title: Pan-Seared Steak with Garlic Butter

ingredients.item: grape tomatoes, diced (seeded if you can)
sea salt, black pepper, dash of oregano

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Serves 2–4; nutrition is per half breast. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, tomatoes, parmesan, basil, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Cut a deep pocket along the long side of each breast, fill with the ricotta mixture, and season.
Press both sides into panko and close with toothpicks.
Brown in the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high 3–4 minutes, flip, and bake 20 minutes until cooked. Rest 5 minutes and slice.
recipes.title: Panko-Crusted Chicken Stuffed with Ricotta, Spinach, Tomato and Basil

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Apps. Calories, protein and weight are estimates per cracker.
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F and set a cooling rack in a foil-lined sheet.
Slice the Parmesan and bacon to match the size of the crackers.
Top each cracker with Parmesan, bacon, brown sugar and pepper flakes, and set on the rack.
Bake 35–45 minutes, rotating halfway (check from 30 minutes), until the bacon is cooked and the edges brown.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.title: Parmesan Candied Bacon Crackers

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. The site lists 286 kcal and 20 g protein, which is too low for up to 2 lb of chicken over 4 servings, so calories, protein and weight are my estimates.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and spray a 9x13.
Toss the vegetables with the oil, half the salt and pepper, 1/4 cup panko, 2 tbsp parmesan and 1 tsp garlic powder, and spread in the dish.
Season the chicken with the rest of the salt and pepper. Dip in egg white, then in the remaining panko mixed with half the remaining parmesan and the rest of the garlic powder. Lay on the vegetables.
Bake 30–40 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are tender. Top with the remaining parmesan.
recipes.title: Parmesan Chicken & Veggie Bake

recipes.notes: From Pinterest board Foods I do like. Nutrition is the site's figure for a 4 oz serving.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment and lay the salmon on it.
Mix the breadcrumbs, parmesan, garlic and herbs. Drizzle with the melted butter, add 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, and mix by hand to coat.
Sprinkle over the salmon and bake 10–12 minutes, until cooked through and golden. If the crust hasn't browned, broil 1 minute. Serve warm.
recipes.title: Parmesan Crusted Salmon

ingredients.item: brown sugar, plus more to garnish (crust)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F and bring a pot of water to a boil.
Blanch the peaches 45 seconds, cool 1 minute, then pit, peel and slice thin.
Divide between two ramekins, add the brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla and flour, and mix. Bake 10 minutes.
Meanwhile cut the butter into the crust dry ingredients until crumbly, then stir in the milk to a wet dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the peaches, sprinkle with brown sugar, and bake 15–20 minutes until bubbly and golden. Serve warm with ice cream.
recipes.title: Peach Cobbler for Two

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Preheat the oven to 350˚F. Lightly grease a 2-quart baking dish with butter and set aside.

Arrange the peach slices on the bottom of the baking dish. Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons of sugar and set aside. Tip: If the peaches are very soft and juicy, toss them with a tablespoon of cornstarch to help thicken the filling.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, 3/4 cup sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Melt the butter, then whisk in the vanilla. Pour the butter mixture over the flour mixture and stir until everything is incorporated and the batter is moist. It will resemble a cookie batter.
Using your hands, sprinkle the batter over the peaches.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until browned on top and bubbly.
Remove from oven and let it rest at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Serve warm with ice cream.
recipes.title: Peach Cobbler Recipe

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories and protein are the site's figures, using full-fat coconut milk; light coconut milk cuts it to about 450 kcal. Weight is an estimate.
steps: Blend everything except the chia seeds until smooth.
Stir the peach mixture and chia seeds together in a glass or bowl.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight, stirring again after 10 minutes to prevent clumps.
Serve with toppings.
recipes.title: Peaches and Cream Chia Pudding (Coconut Milk)

ingredients.item: Double Chocolate Ghirardelli's brownie mix (plus the ingredients the box calls for)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Recipe from the live A Dash of Sanity page (now at dashofsanity.com). Servings and time are the site's. The site lists 352 calories and 8 g protein per serving, which looks too low once the brownie layer and sauce are counted, so calories, protein and serving weight are estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Spray an 8-inch springform (cheesecake) pan with cooking oil. Make the brownies in it according to the package directions, then cool them completely.
Once the brownies are completely cool, make the peanut butter no-bake cheesecake.
Beat the cream cheese, sugar, peanut butter and butter in a large bowl on medium speed until smooth and creamy. Fold in the whipped topping until blended.
Spread the cheesecake mixture on top of the cooled brownies.
Refrigerate until firm and set, 30 to 60 minutes.
About 20 minutes before serving, make the peanut butter hot fudge sauce. (You can make it ahead, refrigerate it, and warm it when ready to use.)

Combine all the sauce ingredients except the vanilla in a medium saucepan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until bubbly, about 5 to 6 minutes. The sauce should be smooth and creamy with no sugar granules left.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla. Let it sit for at least 3 to 5 minutes to cool and thicken.
Cut the cheesecake into slices and serve drizzled with the peanut butter hot fudge sauce.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter & Brownie No-Bake Cheesecake

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. Makes 4 cups (2 large or 4 small bowls). Calories and protein are the site's figures per cup; weight is an estimate.
steps: Run the acai packets under water until partly thawed and add to the blender.
Add the banana, berries, peanut butter, almond milk and honey and blend completely smooth.
Sweeten to taste and add your toppings.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Acai Bowl

ingredients.item: plain yogurt (I used non-fat, you can use other varieties)
honey (optional – feel free to adjust according to taste)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Place all ingredients, except the honey, into your food processor bowl. Process until very smooth.
Taste test the mixture and add honey according to taste (I used 2 tablespoons).
Spoon the mixture into popsicle molds and add sticks according to the instructions of your popsicle mold. Place in freezer and freeze until frozen (overnight is best).
recipes.title: Peanut Butter and Banana Yogurt Pops

ingredients.item: maple syrup (or honey or coconut sugar)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F, line a muffin pan, and mash the bananas in a large bowl.

Eggs (Amount according to the back of the Brownie Mix)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: We like the Ghirardelli Double Chocolate Brownie Mix because of the rich dark chocolate taste and the extra chocolate chips in the batter but go ahead and use your favorite brand of brownie mix. Make up the brownie batter according to the directions on the package and then add 1 cup of Reese's Peanut Butter Chips!
Pour the Brownie batter into a 13" x 9" pan and bake according to the directions on the box. Allow the brownies to completely cool.

While the brownies are cooling, make a batch of our Best Peanut Butter Buttercream Frosting. It is thick, peanut butter-y and so very yummy. You can find the directions to make Best Peanut Butter Buttercream Frosting right here.
Add a thick layer of the Peanut Butter Frosting to the brownies after they are cool.

If you want to make the Brownie Bars a little fancier ... melt 1/2 cup of Semi-Sweet Chocolate Chips in a plastic bag in the microwave. ingredients.item: creamy peanut butter (like Jif or Skippy; not homemade or ‘natural’, it’s too thin and runny)
about 8 ounces (salted) caramel sauce (I used most of a 10-ounce jar of Trader Joe’s Fleur de Sel Caramel Sauce, just eyeball it. Or make Caramel Sauce or make 5-Minute Caramel Sauce
semi-sweet chocolate chips (I used a 9 ounce bag)
vegetable shortening, optional but recommended (for smoothness and so chocolate doesn’t set up overly firm, causing it to crack upon slicing)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Line an 8-inch square baking pan with aluminum foil leaving overhang, spray with cooking spray; set aside. This is a messy recipe and I highly suggest lining your pan for easier cleanup.

Shortbread Crust – Combine all ingredients in a medium mixing bowl, cutting in the butter with a pastry cutter, wooden spoon, or your fingers until until a sandy, crumbly mixture forms. Transfer crumbly mixture to prepared pan and using your fingertips, press crumbs down to form an even flat layer of crust. Pierce crust with a fork haphazardly in a dozen places so steam can escape while it bakes. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, or until crust has just barely set. It should not be golden or browned at all, it should still be white, but crusted over and set. While crust bakes, make the filling.

Peanut Butter Filling – Melt the butter in a medium microwave-safe bowl, about 1 minute. Add the 3 remaining ingredients and stir until smooth. Spread over crust. Crust does not have to be cool, and spreading it while crust is still warm is beneficial. The filling is thick and resists being spread, but take your time and either push it into place with your fingers, use a spatula, or knife, taking care not to rip the crust while spreading the filling.
Caramel Layer – Pour caramel sauce over peanut butter. It should smooth out on its own but if necessary, spread it into corners and sides of pan with a knife.

Chocolate Layer – Combine the 2 ingredients in a medium microwave-safe bowl and heat to melt, about 1 minute. Stop to stir and heat in 15-second bursts until mixture can be stirred smooth. Pour chocolate over caramel layer and if desired, smooth it very, very lightly with an offset spatula or knife.

Cover pan with aluminum foil (to prevent fridge smells), and place pan in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours, or overnight, before lifting out with foil overhang, and slicing and serving. If bars have become very cold, allow them to come up to room temperature for a few minutes before slicing. I prefer to store the bars in the refrigerator, where they’ll keep for at least 10 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months. Crust may lose some degree of snap and crunch if storing the bar for longer durations, but it’s very liveable.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Caramel Twix Bars

ingredients.item: (about 11 ounces bittersweet/dark or semi-sweet chocolate chips)
sour cream or plain greek yogurt

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 9x9” square pan with foil or parchment paper and spray with nonstick cooking spray.

Make the brownie batter: place butter and 1 3/4 cups of the chocolate chips in a large microwave safe bowl. Heat for 1 minute on high power, stir. Continue heating in 30 second increments, stirring between each, until chocolate is melted and smooth. Stir in brown sugar and 1/2 cup granulated sugar. Stir in 3 eggs and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, then add 3/4 cup flour, cocoa powder, and salt and mix until smooth. Set aside.

Make the cheesecake batter: beat cream cheese with a hand or a stand mixer until smooth and creamy. Add peanut butter, 1/4 cup sugar, and sour cream or greek yogurt. Mix until smooth, then add 1 teaspoon vanilla, 1 tablespoon flour, and remaining 2 eggs. Beat until smooth without lumps.

Spread half the brownie batter in the prepared pan. It’s a thick batter but should spread easily with a wooden spoon or spatula. Place half the cheesecake mixture over the top and spread carefully. If you have an offset spatula, that makes spreading this layer easier. Top with remaining brownie batter and then the remaining cheesecake to create 4 layers. Sprinkle with remaining chocolate chips.

Bake for 45-55 minutes until the edges start to get golden and the center is set. Cool completely at room temperature. Chill to set, at least 2 hours or overnight. Cut into small bars and serve. This cheesecake is very rich and a little goes a long way! Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 1 month.

Tablespoons sour cream or Greek yogurt

steps: Line a 8" square baking pan with parchment paper.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
In a mixing bowl, stir together cracker crumbs and melted butter until well combined.Press onto the bottom of the lined pan. Bake for 7 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, mix cream cheese with an electric mixer for 30 seconds, until smooth.
Add peanut butter, sugar,sour cream and vanilla. Mix well.
Add flour. Mix until incorporated.

Pour the mixture over the crust.
Tap the pan against the counter to release any air bubbles.
Bake the cheesecake for 25 to 27 minutes. Let cool completely to room temperature.
It can be chilled overnight.
Drizzle with melted chocolate. Let sit until chocolate is set.
Slice and serve.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Line an 8x8 inch baking pan with foil or parchment paper and set aside.

Allow to cool in the pan, then cut into bars.

recipes.notes: From Pinterest board Foods I do like. Makes about 10 pancakes; 4 servings and the calorie, protein and weight figures are estimates including the syrup.
steps: Preheat a large griddle to medium-high.
In a small bowl, mix the milk, peanut butter, egg and vanilla until smooth.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry and mix until just combined.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour 1/4-cup portions onto the greased griddle.
Flip when the batter starts to bubble, then cook 1–2 minutes more until golden.
For the syrup, stir the maple syrup and peanut butter together and microwave about 30 seconds, then stir.
Pour the syrup over the pancakes. Top with whipped cream, chocolate chips, berries or bananas if you like.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Chocolate Fondue

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 Slice).
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (176°C) and prepare three 8 inch cake pans with non-stick baking spray and parchment paper in the bottom.
Add the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt to a large mixer bowl and combine. Set aside.
Add the milk, vegetable oil, vanilla extract and eggs to a medium sized bowl and combine.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and beat until well combined.
Slowly add the hot water to the batter and mix on low speed until well combined. Scrape down the sides of the bowl as needed to make sure everything is well combined.
Divide the batter evenly between the prepared cake pans and bake for 22-25 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Remove cakes from oven and allow to cool for 2-3 minutes, then remove to a cooling rack to finish cooling.
Combine the butter and peanut butter in a large mixer bowl and mix until well combined.
Add about half of the powdered sugar and mix until smooth.
Add 3 tablespoons of water or milk and mix until smooth.
Add remaining powdered sugar and mix until smooth.
Add remaining water or milk, and salt, and mix until smooth, keeping an eye on the consistency of the frosting so it doesn’t get too thin.
Use a large serrated knife to remove the tops of the cake layers so that they’re flat. See my tips on how to level a cake and how to stack a cake.
Place the first cake layer on a serving plate or cardboard cake circle and top with about 1 cup of frosting. Smooth frosting into an even layer.
Add about half of the chopped Reese’s on top of the frosting and press into the frosting. Spread a small amount of frosting on top of the Reese’s so that it’s sticky on top for the next cake layer.
Add the next cake layer and top with about 1 cup of frosting. Smooth frosting into an even layer.

Add remaining half of the chopped Reese’s on top of the frosting and press into the frosting. Spread a small amount of frosting on top of the Reese’s so that it’s sticky on top for the next cake layer.
Add the final cake layer to the top of the cake.
Smooth out the frosting on the sides of the cake, creating a thin crumb coat.
Add about 1 cup of frosting to the top of the cake and smooth into an even layer.
Frost the cake using my tutorial for a smooth cake. Stop just before using the paper towel, which won’t be necessary with the pattern on the sides of this cake.
Use an offset spatula to create the stripes around the cake. For guidance, see the video above starting at about 1:40.
Set the cake aside and make the chocolate ganache (see my tips for making chocolate ganache).
Put the chocolate chips in a heat proof bowl.
Microwave the heavy whipping cream until it just begins to boil, then pour it over the chocolate chips. Allow it to sit for 2-3 minutes, then whisk until smooth.

Use a squeeze bottle or a spoon to drizzle the chocolate around the edges of the cake, then fill in the top of the cake and smooth it with an offset spatula. See my tips for making a chocolate drip cake.

Allow the ganache to firm a bit, about 10 minutes, then top with swirls of the remaining frosting. Use a piping bag fitted with a closed star tip. I used Ateco tip 844, but Wilton 2D or 1M would work as well. Then top with additional Reese’s chopped in half, and Reese’s crumbles.
Refrigerate the cake until ready to serve. Serve at room temperature. Cake is best for 3-4 days.

Pour over cookie dough crust layer and cover with remaining dough.

ingredients.item: miniature Reese's peanut butter cups, cut into sixths (cheesecake layer)
unsalted butter, room temperature (peanut butter frosting)
good quality semi-sweet chocolate, finely chopped (ganache)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Recipe from the live Family, Food, and Fun blog post. The site gives no servings or nutrition, so servings (16 small slices of a very rich 9-inch cake), time, calories, protein and serving weight are estimates.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan with parchment paper and grease it lightly.
Heat the unsweetened chocolate and butter together in the microwave or a small saucepan until the butter melts, then stir until the chocolate is completely melted.
Stir in the sugar (the mixture will be grainy). Stir in the eggs and vanilla, then add the flour and stir just until combined.
Spread in the prepared pan and bake 25 to 30 minutes, until a toothpick comes out nearly clean; don't overbake. Cool completely and remove from the pan.
Prepare the springform pan again the same way for the cheesecake.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar with an electric mixer until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing slowly after each, then stir in the vanilla.
Pour the cheesecake into the pan, sprinkle the peanut butter cup pieces over the top and gently press some into the batter.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the center is just set. Cool completely, remove from the pan, and wrap in foil to refrigerate or freeze if making ahead.

For the frosting, beat the powdered sugar, peanut butter, butter, vanilla and salt with the paddle attachment on medium-low until creamy, scraping down the bowl. Add the cream and beat on high until light and smooth.
For the ganache, put the chopped chocolate in a bowl. Heat the cream just until simmering and pour it over the chocolate. Let it sit a few minutes, stir until melted, and cool to room temperature.
To assemble, put a dab of frosting on the serving plate and set the brownie on it. Spread a 1/2-inch layer of peanut butter frosting over the brownie.
Place the cheesecake on top, trimming any brownie edges that stick out past it.
Pour the ganache over the cheesecake, letting some drip over the edges if you like, and refrigerate a few minutes to let the chocolate firm up.
Pipe the rest of the peanut butter frosting in swirls on top and around the edges. Garnish with extra peanut butter cups if you like.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cup Brownie Cheesecake (Rebekah's)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Combine the cream, milk, peanut butter and both sugars in a medium saucepan. Place the pan over medium heat and warm the mixture, whisking frequently, until the sugars dissolve and the peanut butter melts into the cream. It doesn't need to come to a boil—as soon as the mixture is smooth and homogenous, you can remove it from the heat. Whisk in the vanilla extract.
Pour it into a bowl or plastic container, and place it in the refrigerator until chilled. If you want to speed this process up, place the bowl over an ice bath and whisk it as it cools down.

Once the peanut butter mixture is chilled, pour it into your ice cream maker and churn according to manufacturer's directions, until it is the consistency of soft-serve ice cream. Stir in the miniature peanut butter cups by hand.

If you want to add a fudge and/or peanut butter swirl, spread about a third of the peanut butter ice cream in the bottom of a 9x5-inch loaf pan. Drizzle the peanut butter sauce over the ice cream, then top it with half the remaining ice cream. Drizzle the fudge sauce over this, and finish by covering it with the rest of the ice cream. (If you're omitting the swirls, simply spread all of the ice cream into the loaf pan.) Press a layer of cling wrap on top, and freeze the pan until the ice cream is firm, about 2 hours.

regular Reese's peanut butter cups, chopped (or 20 small)

ingredients.item: plain or vanilla yogurt of choice
peanut butter, or allergy friendly sub
if using plain yogurt, add 1 tsp pure vanilla extract

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: *Feel free to use your favorite sweetener, such as pure maple syrup, regular sugar or coconut sugar, or erythritol for sugar free. Or skip the sweetener and blend in an overripe banana or dates as desired. If using a liquid sweetener, omit the milk of choice.Whisk ingredients until completely smooth. If you have an ice cream maker, churn according to machine directions. If you don’t, you can either freeze in an ice cube tray and later blend the frozen ice cubes in a vitamix or high-quality food processor until completely smooth OR you can freeze the mixture in a container, taking it out to stir every twenty minutes (being sure to scrape the sides of the container as you stir) until it is thick and smooth. The third way won’t get quite as smooth as the first two methods, but all three of the methods yield delicious results! Because of the lack of preservatives or gums, the frozen yogurt has the best smooth and creamy texture the day it’s made. However, you can technically freeze leftovers for a few weeks in an airtight container, thawing at least ten minutes before eating. View Nutrition Facts
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Frozen Yogurt

steps: Cream the peanut butter and sugar in a stand mixer on medium about 1 minute.
Add the milk and mix on low 2–3 minutes until smooth and thinned, then mix in the cream about 30 seconds.
Churn in an ice cream maker (about 25 minutes) to soft-serve consistency.
Fold in the chopped peanut butter cups and freeze in an airtight container up to a week.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Ice Cream with Chopped Peanut Butter Cups

ingredients.item: semi-sweet chocolate chips, (divided into ¾ cup and 1 cup (Ghirardelli brand 12-ounce bag))

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Line 12 standard-sized muffin cups with cupcake liners. Set aside.

In a small microwave-safe bowl, place ¾ cup semi-sweet chocolate chips. Melt the chocolate by heating it in 30-second intervals and stirring in between until the chocolate is smooth. Depending on how your microwave heats, this should take 1½ to 2 minutes.

Scoop out about ½ tablespoon of melted chocolate into each cupcake liner. This can be done by scooping the chocolate with a small spoon and scraping it off with another. You may need to use a spoon to gently spread the chocolate into an even layer, being careful not to get any on the upper sides of the paper liners.
Freeze the chocolate for 10 minutes.

While the chocolate is freezing, prepare the peanut butter filling. Measure the peanut butter, powdered sugar, and unsalted butter into a medium mixing bowl. Using a handheld mixer, on medium speed, beat until the peanut butter mixture is smooth.

Scoop 2 teaspoons of the peanut butter filling onto the center of the chocolate layer. Using a spoon, gently flatten and spread the filling into an even layer, being sure that the filling does not touch the sides of the cupcake liner. Freeze for an additional 10 minutes.

Remove from the freezer and top each peanut butter cup with 1 teaspoon of the marshmallow creme, being sure to keep the marshmallow creme in the center of the peanut butter cup. Lightly wet your fingertip and smooth down the marshmallow creme. Freeze again for another 10 minutes.
Just before your marshmallow creme layer is done freezing, melt the remaining 1 cup of semi-sweet chocolate chips (using the same bowl from step 2) in the same way as explained in step 2.

Using the two-spoon method from step 3, cover the peanut butter and marshmallow creme with the melted chocolate. You will need to use the back of one spoon to push the melted chocolate all the way to the edges and completely cover the top.
Freeze for a final 10 minutes to set and harden the top layer of chocolate.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Marshmallow Cups

steps: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees.

Add the oats, baking powder, and salt and mix again to combine.
Fold the chocolate chips into the batter.
Use a mini cookie scoop to portion the batter onto a non stick baking sheet. Use a fork to shape and slightly flatten the batter into a cookie shape (they will not spread much).
Bake the flourless cookies at 350 degrees for 8-13 minutes, until the edges are set and the bottoms are browned.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cookies

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Snacks. Makes 18; a serving is 3 muffins (the blogger's figure is 83 kcal and 6.4 g protein per muffin). The live recipe card doesn't load, so this comes from a 2025 web archive copy. Weight is an estimate.

Cool 5–10 minutes before removing. Keeps about a week in the fridge; best warmed.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Protein Snack Muffins

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. The live recipe card didn't load, so this comes from a 2021 web archive copy. Calories are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Grease a 10x15x1 inch jellyroll pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt.
Combine 1 1/2 sticks butter and 1 cup water in a medium saucepan and bring to a simmer. Sitr to make sure all butter is melted.
Whisk 1/2 cup peanut butter and vegetable oil into butter mixture. Stir into flour mixture.
Whisk together eggs, buttermilk, and vanilla extract. Stir into flour mixture until well combined.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake for 22 to 26 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in middle comes out clean. Let cool.
To make frosting, use an electric mixer to beat butter and peanut butter together until smooth.
Add half of confectioners' sugar and half of milk and beat until smooth.
Add remaining confectioners' sugar, milk and the vanilla pudding mix and beat until smooth. Add a little more milk if necessary.
Spread frosting on cake.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Sheet Cake

ingredients.item: vanilla plant-based protein powder (she used Sunwarrior)
creamy unsalted peanut butter, for the swirl

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. The live page is gone, so this comes from a 2020 web archive copy. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F and spray a good nonstick 12-cup muffin tin well (or use foil or silicone cups); oat muffins like to stick.
Whisk the bananas, peanut butter, milk, applesauce and vanilla in a large bowl.
Gently stir in the protein powder, oats, baking powder, baking soda and cinnamon (the batter is thick).
Fill each cup about 2/3 full, top each with 1 tsp peanut butter, and swirl with a toothpick.
Bake 20 minutes, then cool in the tin at least 45 minutes before moving to a rack (they get less crumbly as they cool).
Keep airtight up to 3 days, or 5–6 days in the fridge.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Swirl Banana Protein Muffins

ingredients.item: Joy Filled Eats Sweetener (or see alternatives in recipe notes)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (0.5 cup).
steps: Combine coconut milk, almond milk, and the sweetener in a saucepan over low heat. Simmer for 1 hour or until reduced by 1/4.

Put the egg yolks in a large glass bowl. While whisking vigorously slowly pour the hot milk mixture over the yolks. Add the raw cocoa butter and 1/3 cup of the peanut butter and stir until the cocoa butter melts and the mixture is smooth.

Chill for 6-8 hours. Pour into a 2-quart ice cream machine and churn according to the manufacturer's instructions. If your ice cream machine is smaller then 2 qt. you will have to churn this in 2 batches. Or make some into ice cream and some into ice pops. When the ice cream has finished churning gently swirl in the remaining peanut butter. Freeze until firm.
If this hardens in the freezer simply leave out at room temperature for 15-30 minutes to soften before serving.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Swirl Ice Cream

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Combine the flour, sugar, salt and baking soda in a large bowl.
Bring the butter, water and peanut butter to a boil in a saucepan and mix into the flour mixture.
Mix the eggs, vanilla and milk and stir in.
Spread in a greased 15x10 jelly roll pan and bake at 350°F for 15–20 minutes.
For the icing, boil the butter, peanut butter and milk, then off the heat stir in the powdered sugar and vanilla. Spread over the warm cake.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter Texas Sheet Cake

ingredients.item: Betty Crocker™ Super Moist™ chocolate fudge cake mix
Water, vegetable oil and eggs called for on cake mix box
(8 oz) Cool Whip frozen whipped topping, thawed
Reese's peanut butter cups miniatures, unwrapped

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. The live recipe card didn't load, so this comes from a 2021 web archive copy. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 Serving).
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (325°F for dark or nonstick pans). Grease and lightly flour 13x9-inch pan. Make and bake cake as directed on box for 13x9-inch pan. Cool completely in pan.
Poke holes in cake using fork or skewer. Pour 3/4 cup of the chocolate syrup over cake; let stand until most of the syrup soaks into cake.
In large bowl, beat peanut butter and whipped topping with electric mixer on medium speed until combined. Spread over cake.
Using large chef’s knife, cut peanut butter cups into fourths. Scatter over frosting. Drizzle with remaining 1/4 cup chocolate syrup.
Cover and refrigerate cake, but bring to room temperature before serving. Cover and refrigerate any remaining cake.
recipes.title: Peanut Butter-Chocolate Poke Cake

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Asian. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Whisk the sauce ingredients.
Boil the soba 2–3 minutes until al dente, saving a cup of the water, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Cook the chicken in 1 tbsp oil in a hot wok 7–8 minutes until golden, add a third of the sauce, and stir until it thickens.
Add the other 1 tbsp oil and the peppers and cook 3–4 minutes.
Lower to medium, add the kale, noodles and the rest of the sauce, and toss about a minute (thin with noodle water if needed).
Top with peanuts, green onions and pepper flakes.
recipes.title: Peanut Chicken Soba Noodle Stir Fry

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Lunch. The live recipe card doesn't load, so this comes from a 2018 web archive copy. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Cook the chicken in 1 tbsp oil in a wok until no longer pink; set aside.
Cook the vegetables 5–7 minutes.
Whisk the sauce, return the chicken, pour the sauce over, and stir until combined.
Microwave the cauliflower rice and divide everything among 4 containers. Refrigerate and reheat.
recipes.title: Peanut Chicken Stir Fry Meal Prep Bowls

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 9x13-inch pan with foil and spray with nonstick cooking spray.

Place pecans in a small frying pan and heat over medium low heat, stirring often, until toasted, about 3-5 minutes. Don’t walk away or they’ll burn – as soon as you smell them they’re done. Remove from pan to a plate to cool completely.
Cream butter and sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer. Mix in vanilla, salt, then cornstarch. Slowly mix in flour until combined, then stir in toasted pecans.
Press dough into a thin layer in prepared pan. Bake for 25-30 minutes for soft-baked or up to 35 minutes for crunchy.
Cool completely before slicing into bars. Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
recipes.title: Pecan Shortbread Bars Recipe

ingredients.item: olive oil, plus more for drizzling
chili flakes or crushed red pepper, plus more

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Pasta. Calories and protein are the site's figures; serving weight is an estimate.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet until shimmering, add the garlic and chili flakes, and cook over medium heat about 60 seconds without browning the garlic.
Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook over medium heat 15 minutes, breaking up the tomatoes, until slightly reduced.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente.
Reserve about 1/4 cup pasta water, then drain.
Season the sauce and stir in the pasta and parsley.
Toss well, loosening with pasta water if needed.
Serve with a drizzle of olive oil and more parsley or cheese.
recipes.title: Penne all'Arrabbiata

ingredients.item: red pepper flakes, salt and pepper (sauce)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. The site lists 660 kcal per roll, which is too high for these ingredients over 10 rolls, so calories, protein and weight are my estimates.
steps: Sauce: cook the garlic and onion in the butter and oil over medium-low 5 minutes, stir in the tomatoes, paste, herbs, sugar and pepper flakes, bring to a boil, and simmer 15 minutes. Blend to the texture you like (it makes extra).
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lay the cooked noodles on wax paper. Spread 1/2 cup pizza sauce in a sprayed baking dish.
Mix the egg, ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, 1/2 cup parmesan, parsley and pepper.
Spread each noodle with about 2 tbsp filling, add 5–6 pepperoni, roll up, and set seam side down in the dish.
Top with sauce and the remaining cheeses, cover with foil, and bake 45–50 minutes (uncover for the last 10–15). Rest 10 minutes.
recipes.title: Pepperoni Pizza Lasagna Rolls

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Put everything in a large greased slow cooker (7-quart).
Cook on Low 9–10 hours or High 6–8.
Shred and serve with the gravy, over mashed potatoes or on toasted hoagie rolls.
recipes.title: Perfect 4-Ingredient Slow Cooker Pot Roast

ingredients.item: powdered sugar (depending on your desired consistency and sweetness of frosting)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Using an electric hand mixer (or stand mixer with paddle attachment), beat together the butter and the cream cheese. Slowly and gradually blend in the powdered sugar and vanilla, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed. Then beat on high until well-combined, smooth, and creamy.

Cream Cheese Frosting should be stored in the refrigerator. You can either apply the frosting as soon as you make it and then refrigerate your cake/cupcakes/etc., or transfer the frosting to a sealed container, refrigerate, and then bring to room temperature and stir until smooth before using.
recipes.title: PERFECT Cream Cheese Frosting (Quick, Easy, Versatile)

(150 g) coconut sugar or brown sugar
(98 g) natural almond butter, room temperature
egg, room temperature (or a chia egg)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Stir together the almond flour, coconut flour, baking soda and salt.
Beat the fat and sugar about 1 minute, then the almond butter and vanilla, then the egg on low.
Stir in the flour mixture, then 1 cup chocolate chips. If you used coconut sugar, chill the dough about an hour.
Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet. Roll 8 large (75 g) balls, press the remaining chips onto them, space 4 inches apart, and flatten slightly.
Bake 11–14 minutes with coconut sugar or 14–17 with brown sugar.
recipes.title: Perfect Paleo Chocolate Chip Cookies

steps: Blend everything until smooth.

steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Mix the sugars, spice and salt.
Mix the eggs and pumpkin, then stir in the sugar mixture until smooth, then slowly stir in the evaporated milk.
Pour into the pie shell and bake on a small sheet pan at 400°F for 15 minutes, then at 375°F for 35–45 minutes until set.
Cool and top with whipped cream.
recipes.title: Perfect Pumpkin Pie

recipes.notes: From Pinterest board Foods I do like. Calories and protein are Food.com's figures; serving weight is an estimate for 1 pepper half.
steps: Halve the peppers lengthwise and remove the ribs and seeds.
Slice the onion and mushrooms and sauté over medium heat in the butter and olive oil with the garlic and a little salt and pepper until caramelized, 25–30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Slice the roast beef into thin strips, add to the onions and mushrooms and cook 5–10 minutes.
Line the inside of each pepper half with a slice of provolone.
Fill each pepper until nearly overflowing with the meat mixture.
Top each with another slice of provolone.
Bake 15–20 minutes until the cheese is golden brown.
recipes.title: Philly Cheesesteak Stuffed Peppers

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. The page is gone, so this comes from a 2014 web archive copy (originally from Peace Love & Low Carb). Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Halve the peppers lengthwise and remove the ribs and seeds.
Sauté the onions and mushrooms in the butter, oil and garlic with salt and pepper over medium until caramelized, 25–30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Add the roast beef in thin strips and cook 5–10 minutes.
Line each pepper half with provolone, fill with the meat mixture, and top with another slice.
Bake 15–20 minutes until the cheese is golden.
recipes.title: Philly Cheesesteak Stuffed Peppers (Low Carb)

ingredients.item: green onions, finely chopped (or a small onion)
teriyaki sauce, plus more to serve

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Mix everything except the pineapple and buns and chill until ready to grill.
Shape into patties and grill over 350°F heat 7–10 minutes per side, flipping once.
For the last 5 minutes, grill the pineapple 2–3 minutes per side.
Serve on buns topped with pineapple, extra teriyaki and green onions.
recipes.title: Pineapple Teriyaki Pork Burgers

steps: Sauté the onion in the oil over medium-high 4–5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, garlic, carrots, potato and spices for 1–2 minutes, then add the broth and bay leaves.
Boil, then simmer covered 10–15 minutes. Add the beans and cook 10 minutes more, adding broth if needed.
Blend about half the soup and stir it back in.
Season, add a squeeze of lime if you like, and garnish with herbs.

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Pasta. Makes 2 casseroles of 10 servings each; freeze one for later. Calories and protein are the site's figures; serving weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Brown the beef and onion in a large skillet and drain.
Stir in the spaghetti sauce and pasta.
Divide between two greased 13x9 dishes, sprinkle with cheese, and arrange the pepperoni on top.
Bake uncovered 25–30 minutes until heated through.
recipes.title: Pizza Pasta Casserole

ingredients.item: cooked sausage or other pizza toppings

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Dinner. Calories and protein are the site's figures, without toppings; weight is an estimate.
steps: Spread some sauce on one tortilla, sprinkle with cheese and toppings, and cover with the second tortilla.
Spray the pan, add the pizzadilla, and spray the top.
Cook over medium until golden and melted, flipping once.
Cut into wedges and dip in the remaining sauce.
recipes.title: Pizzadillas (Pizza Quesadillas)

ingredients.item: mini semi-sweet chocolate chips (may sub regular)

recipes.notes: Optionally microwave a serving for about 15 seconds before eating. Total time estimated from bake time plus cooling and caramel setting time; servings, serving weight, calories and protein are estimates.
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Line a 9x13 pan with parchment paper or aluminum foil so it overhangs slightly, and lightly spray with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, mix together flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon. Set aside.
In a separate large bowl, whisk butter, sugar and cocoa powder together.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each addition just until incorporated, then beat in vanilla.
Fold in the flour mixture just until combined.
Stir in 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips and 3/4 cup chopped pecans until just combined.
Pour batter evenly into the pan.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes.
Let the pan cool on a wire rack for 5 minutes, then poke holes all over with the back of a chopstick or small wooden spoon.
Pour 1/2 cup caramel over the brownies and spread it into the holes with a spatula.
Refrigerate for one hour or freeze for 30 minutes to let the caramel set, and meanwhile make the frosting.
For the frosting, beat butter, cocoa, corn syrup and vanilla in a small bowl until blended.
Add powdered sugar and 2 tablespoons milk and beat until smooth, adding more milk if needed to reach spreading consistency.
Once the caramel has set, frost the brownies with the chocolate frosting (you don't have to use all of it).
Sprinkle evenly with 1/2 cup chopped pecans and 1/4 cup mini chocolate chips, and drizzle with 1/4 cup caramel.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate to let the frosting set and make cutting easier.
recipes.title: Poke Turtle Brownies

ingredients.item: frozen mixed vegetables, thawed and well drained

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Casseroles. Calories and protein are the site's figures; serving weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Bring the water and salt to a boil, reduce to a gentle boil and slowly whisk in the cornmeal. Cook and stir 15–20 minutes until thick and pulling away from the pan.
Stir in 1/4 cup cheddar until melted.
Spread in a greased 13x9 dish and bake uncovered 20 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the chili.
Spread the vegetables over the polenta, top with the chili and the remaining cheese, and bake 12–15 minutes until melted. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.title: Polenta Chili Casserole

ingredients.item: baked sweet potato (no skin), from about 2 large sweet potatoes
quinoa flour (or oat flour, oatmeal ground into flour)
zucchini, grated (optional, but recommended since it adds moisture)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. The live page lists only the steps, so the ingredient list came from an archived copy (web.archive.org, October 2021). Servings (12), time, calories (121) and protein (5 g) are the site's; serving weight is an estimate.
steps: Set the oven to 415°F.
Bake 2 large sweet potatoes until soft, about 1 hour. Let them cool to room temperature.
Set the oven to 350°F.
Grate the zucchini into a bowl and set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, add the sweet potato and mash.
Add all the remaining ingredients and mix together thoroughly.
Divide the batter evenly among the cups of a muffin pan.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the brownies comes out clean. Let cool; they keep in the fridge for up to a week.
recipes.title: Post-Workout Sweet Potato Brownies (Fit Men Cook)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. The site has expired, so this comes from a 2019 web archive copy. Calories, protein and weight are estimates (with cheese).
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
If making mashed potatoes: peel and cube potatoes, boil about 10 minutes until fork-tender, drain, and mash smooth with salt and pepper.
Line muffin cups with the mashed potatoes or hash browns.
Whisk the eggs with the remaining ingredients and spoon into the centers.
Bake 15–20 minutes. Makes 8; reheat about 45 seconds in the microwave.
recipes.title: Potato Egg Cups

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 brownie).
steps: Preheat the oven to 180C/350F. Line an 8 x 8-inch pan with parchment paper and set aside.
In a high speed blender or mixing bowl, combine all your ingredients and blend or mix until smooth.
Transfer the brownie batter to the lined pan and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the tops are firm.
Remove the brownies from the oven and gently press down on the tops to form a crackly top. Let them cool completely before slicing and serving.

1 tsp each salt, garlic powder, onion powder; 1/2 tsp paprika; 1/4 tsp pepper

Add everything else except the pasta.
Cook on high 3–4 hours or low 6–8.
Shred the chicken and return it, then stir in the pasta and cook on high 10–20 minutes until tender. Remove the bay leaf.

Instant Pot: sauté the vegetables in 1 tbsp oil 5–7 minutes, add the garlic, broth (scrape the bottom), seasonings and chicken. Cook on high pressure 20 minutes with a 10-minute natural release. Shred the chicken, add the pasta, and cook on warm 10–15 minutes.
recipes.title: Protein Packed Slow Cooker Chicken Noodle Soup

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Mix the cocoa, yogurt and protein powder, adding water a tablespoon at a time until pourable.
Separately mix the PB2 with water until pourable.
Pour chocolate a quarter of the way up each liner, then the PB2 mixture, then top with more chocolate (don't overfill).
Freeze about 15 minutes. Store leftovers in the freezer.
recipes.title: Protein Peanut Butter Cups (Clean Eating)

ingredients.item: add-ins of choice (berries, chocolate chips, nuts, etc.)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories, protein and weight are estimates, without add-ins.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Combine the oats, protein powder, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In another bowl, combine the eggs, vanilla, applesauce, yogurt, coconut oil, honey and almond milk.
Stir the wet into the dry.
Grease a muffin pan very well with coconut oil and divide the batter among the cups.
Stir your add-ins into each cup and sprinkle with hemp seeds.

recipes.title: Protein-Packed Baked Oatmeal Cups

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Apps. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Cut each pastry sheet into 2 rectangles and whisk the egg with the water.
Mix the sausage, salt, pepper, cream cheese, jalapeños and onion and divide into 4.
Roll each portion into a log down the middle of a pastry piece, brush the edges with egg, fold over, and pinch to seal.
Cut each log into 4–8 pieces, set seam side down, and brush with egg.
Bake 20–25 minutes until golden. Serve with ketchup, mustard, BBQ or marinara.
recipes.title: Puff Pastry Sausage Rolls with Jalapeño Cream Cheese

ingredients.item: apple, peeled and diced (e.g. Pink Lady)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease an 8x8 pan.
Beat the pumpkin, banana, eggs, coconut milk, pumpkin spice, 1/2 tsp cinnamon and salt with a hand mixer or immersion blender.
Toss the apple with the remaining cinnamon, fold it in, and pour into the pan.
Scatter the pecans over the top.
Bake 35–40 minutes until mostly firm and golden on top.
Rest at least 10 minutes. Keeps a week in the fridge; serve warm, cold or at room temperature.
recipes.title: Pumpkin Apple Breakfast Bake (Paleo, Whole30)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch loaf pan well.
Beat all the bread ingredients with a hand mixer until well mixed and pour into the pan.
Bake 40–50 minutes until a toothpick near the center comes out mostly clean. Cool 15 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.
Melt the butter over medium-low and keep cooking 4–5 minutes until amber and nutty; cool completely.
Stir in the powdered sugar and maple syrup (thin with milk if needed), pour over the loaf, and let set about 30 minutes.
recipes.title: Pumpkin Bread with Brown Butter Maple Icing

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Breakfast. Calories and protein are the site's figures; weight is an estimate.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Combine both oats, the cranberries, pumpkin seeds, flax, spice and salt. Stir in the pumpkin, eggs, coconut oil and honey until fully combined.
Scoop 1/4-cup mounds onto the sheet (tap the packed cup out so it keeps its shape).
Flatten slightly (they won't spread) and bake 15–20 minutes until the edges are lightly browned.
Cool on the sheet, then store airtight.
recipes.title: Pumpkin Breakfast Cookies (Cranberry & Pepita)

ingredients.item: pumpkin pie spice (optional, or ground cinnamon and a pinch of nutmeg)
pumpkin puree (do not use pumpkin pie filling)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1).
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F. Butter and flour three 8-inch round cake pans or spray them with non-stick baking spray like Baker's Joy. Set aside. You can also use 9-inch round cake pans, keep an eye on them though as they will bake faster!
In a medium bowl, mix flour, baking soda, pumpkin pie spice, and salt. Set aside.

In a large bowl/stand mixer, cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in vanilla, pumpkin, and vegetable oil. Beat in the flour mixture alternately with the milk until just combined. Do not over mix the batter!

Divide batter evenly into prepared pans. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean. Remove pans from oven and immediately place in freezer for 45 minutes. (You can also let them cool at room temperature on the counter. However, popping them into the freezer stops the cooking process much faster and keeps this cake super moist!)
In a large bowl, cream butter and cream cheese until smooth. Beat in maple syrup, vanilla and cinnamon. Add powdered sugar and beat on low speed until combined, then on high until frosting is smooth.
Assemble the 3 layers with a thick layer of frosting in between each layer. Apply one final thick and even layer around the outside of the cake.

Store frosted cake in the fridge until ready to serve in an airtight container or lightly covered with plastic wrap or foil. Allow the cake to warm up a little at room temperature before serving for the best texture.
recipes.title: Pumpkin Cake with Cinnamon Cream Cheese Frosting

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Anti-Inflammatory. Calories, protein and weight are estimates.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and line 9 muffin cups.
Whisk the wet ingredients, then whisk in the dry ingredients just until combined.
Fill each cup with about 1/4 cup batter and bake 20 minutes. Cool completely on a rack.
Whisk the coconut cream, maple syrup and vanilla until smooth, then whisk in the tapioca.
Pipe onto the cooled cupcakes.
recipes.title: Pumpkin Cassava Flour Cupcakes (Paleo, Nut-Free)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are my estimates from the ingredients.
steps: Beat the cream cheese, sugar, sour cream and pumpkin until smooth.
Beat in the milk, pumpkin pie spice and salt.
Churn in an ice cream maker per its directions.
recipes.title: Pumpkin Cheesecake Ice Cream

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 serving).
steps: Whisk 3¾ cups all-purpose flour, 1½ teaspoons baking powder, ½ teaspoon salt, ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon, and ¼ teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a mixer with a paddle attachment, beat together 1 cup unsalted butter, 1 cup granulated sugar, and ½ cup light brown sugar on medium-high speed until fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.
Blend in ¾ cup pumpkin puree, beat in 1 large egg, and then add 2 teaspoons vanilla extract. Slowly add dry ingredients on low speed just until combined. Cover and chill the dough for an hour.
Blend 8 ounces cream cheese,1/4 cup granulated sugar, and 2 teaspoons vanilla extract together to make the cream cheese filling. Chill for one hour.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit and line your baking sheets with parchment paper. In a small bowl, combine ½ cup granulated sugar, 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, ½ teaspoon ground gingerand a dash allspice for the coating and set aside.

To make the cookies, take a tablespoon of the cookie dough. Flatten it like a pancake and place a teaspoon of the cream cheese in the center. Form another tablespoon of the cookie batter into a flat pancake shape and place it on top of the cream cheese. Pinch the edges together, sealing in the cream cheese, and roll into a ball. Roll in the cinnamon sugar coating and place on the prepared baking sheet 2 inches apart.
Repeat until the dough is gone, and flatten the cookie dough balls with a heavy bottomed glass or measuring cup.
Bake the cookies for 10-15 minutes or until the tops start to crack. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes and transfer to a wire rack. Enjoy!
recipes.title: Pumpkin Cheesecake Snickerdoodles

ingredients.item: salt (or 1/2 teaspoon if using unsalted butter)

recipes.notes: From Jessica Lynn's Pinterest board Desserts. Calories and protein are the site's figures per serving (1 g).
steps: Preheat oven to 350°.
In a large bowl, combine pumpkin puree, brown sugar, milk, and oil. Stir well.
